findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed staff failure to use a barrier to shut off the faucet after handwashing. Discussed with PIC and education was carried out to correct the behavior. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable to use a barrier to shut the faucet after handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The internal surface of the dish machine in the kitchen was observed with a buildup of soil accumulation. 
PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the above mentioned surfaces would be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ones mentioned are monitored, cleaned, sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: The temperatures of the cut veggies in the prep cooler in the serving area were observed out of the appropriate range. PIC told inspector that all the food items in the unit may have been placed in the unit between last night and 9:00 AM today. The carrots were measured at 54 F and Celery was measured at 53 F.  The carrots (two trays) and celery (two trays and half a bag) were tossed. Ensure that chopped ready to eat food items are held within the appropriate temperature range to avoid bacteria growth.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The prep cooler holding vegetables in the serving area was observed to not be holding temperature. The ambient temperature in the unit using an infrared thermometer was 61. The food items probed in the unit was temped at 53.5 on average. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the unit will be repaired within the follow-up timeframe. Ensure that the temperature of cold holding units are checked on a regular basis.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a couple boxes of food items being stored on the floor in the walk-in freezer. PIC was made aware. The boxes were removed to be stored properly. Ensure that food items are stored at least 6 inches above the floor to avoid contamination through splash at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the top of the kitchen dish machine to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning dish machine at a frequency that prevents food accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
